mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly orders the metals according to their observed reactivity with water, from most vigorous to least vigorous?
mcqs.explanation: Alkali metals react most vigorously with water. Potassium reacts more violently than sodium, followed by calcium (which reacts slowly), magnesium (very slow or no visible reaction), and iron (no reaction). Option B reflects this correct order.

mcqs.question: Which metal does NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid under normal laboratory conditions?
mcqs.explanation: Copper is placed below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Zinc, iron, and magnesium are above hydrogen and readily evolve H₂ gas when treated with the acid.

mcqs.question: When a metal reacts with an acid, which gas is most commonly liberated?
mcqs.explanation: Metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series displace hydrogen ions from acids, producing hydrogen gas (H₂). The other gases listed are not typical products of metal‑acid reactions.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: According to the reactivity series, which metal can be used to displace copper from an aqueous CuSO₄ solution?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc lies above copper in the reactivity series, so it can displace copper ions, forming ZnSO₄ and depositing metallic copper. Copper itself cannot displace copper, and gold and silver are less reactive than copper.

mcqs.question: Which statement best distinguishes the reaction of sodium with water from that of iron with water?

options.A: Both metals produce a colourless gas, but only iron forms a protective oxide layer.
options.B: Sodium reacts vigorously, producing NaOH and H₂, whereas iron shows practically no reaction.
options.C: Iron reacts vigorously, producing Fe(OH)₂ and H₂, while sodium forms a passive film.
options.D: Both metals react slowly, but sodium releases oxygen instead of hydrogen.

mcqs.answer: Sodium reacts vigorously, producing NaOH and H₂, whereas iron shows practically no reaction.
mcqs.explanation: Alkali metal sodium reacts explosively with water, forming sodium hydroxide and hydrogen gas. Iron, a transition metal, does not react noticeably with cold water under normal conditions.

mcqs.question: A student adds a small piece of metal X to dilute HCl and observes rapid bubbling and the solution turning colourless. Which metal is most likely X?
mcqs.explanation: Zinc is above hydrogen in the reactivity series and reacts readily with dilute HCl, producing ZnCl₂ and hydrogen gas (visible as bubbles). Copper and gold do not react, and lead reacts only very slowly.

mcqs.question: When a strip of magnesium ribbon is placed in dilute hydrochloric acid, which gas is evolved?
mcqs.explanation: Magnesium is more reactive than hydrogen; it displaces hydrogen ions from HCl, forming MgCl₂ and releasing hydrogen gas. The other gases are not products of this reaction.

mcqs.learning_point: Use the reactivity series to predict reactions
mcqs.question: A piece of metal Y is immersed in an aqueous solution of AgNO₃. After a few minutes, a silver coating appears on the surface of Y. Which metal could be Y?
mcqs.explanation: Copper lies above silver in the reactivity series, so it can displace silver ions from AgNO₃, depositing metallic silver on its surface and forming Cu(NO₃)₂ in solution. Gold, lead, and mercury are less reactive than silver and cannot cause this displacement.
